content.label: I’m a huge fan of Gentler Streak and am a beta tester. I’ve been using the new sleep features for awhile now and love them. Every morning I check in to see how I’m doing. Other than sleep, I use the app to track my workouts in Apple Fitness+ as well as walking my dog and kayaking (the watch app is phenomenal for kayaking). Staying within my path is so much better than being preoccupied with closing rings which sometimes isn’t the best thing for us. Sometimes rest and recovery is most important and GS lets me know how I’m doing. It’s a stunningly beautiful and thoughtful app. The most important app I own.

title.label: Drains the crap out of my watch

content.label:
i have a series 7 apple watch, needed an upgrade so a month or so ago, I treated myself to a brand new watch. 
Normally with my apple watch, i could easily go over a day without having to recharge my watch.

Ever since the day install this app onto my watch … I **LITERALLY** HAVE TO CHARGE MY WATCH [AT LEAST 2 TIMES PER DAY. 

I simply can’t justify paying $15/month for this app… not sure why it drained the battery so dramatically, but until that is fixed, I’m gonna have to give it two stars. 

The second reason why I’m giving it to stars is because of how hard it was to navigate and understand that I have initially within the first few days I bought it. 

Id really like a refund… but at this point, I think it’s too late… 
it’s a pretty decent app honestly. 
and if it doesn’t drain your battery life and you’re able to quickly understand how to navigate the app both on your phone and your watch. I think this could be potentially amazing app! 

but with a few tweaks, it could be an amazing one .
Hard to get motivated with this app. With every workout regardless of intensity or frequency, it says you’re overreaching.

After updating the app in iOS 18 the widget on Lock Screen goes away. I couldn’t find a way to bring back. 
Note I’ve an iphone11
I bought it. But I’ve never gotten a notice or a push or anything, it’s just running out it’s time

I came across the app by chance. It felt like a good fit. I run-ish. And walk a lot. Often solo. Am mature!  Liked the idea of advice and nudging. What  a good choice. My husband got interested when I passed the first free week and signed up for the year. He decided he’d give it a go. His first week a success. Then to get him covered by my family account. That was our stumbling block. Tried so hard to work out how to include him as family. Vid to the rescue. What a super-patient professional he was. We exchanged emails mercilessly!  Got there in the end. Two very happy campers now in the ‘Gentle’ club. And most happy to be there. Thank you Vid particularly. What service. I’d not have dreamed it possible. It will take some time to learn the bells and whistles of the app. But slowly, slowly … and enjoying the ideas and challenge. 💯 recommended.

I was using the app for a while and I genuinely like it. I think the visuals are very pretty and the “band” approach to streak is a healthier way to fitness compared to normal apple watch rings. You can take days off if needed but it’s still insanely satisfying to push that band up. I like the monthly summary and always look forward to seeing that widget on the first day of the month.

To developers: keep up the good work! I love seeing the charts and stats and would like even more insights.

I pay for this app a year ago for X amount of dollars and then when I went to renew it they offered me a 40% discount to renew and so I paid it and somehow ended up losing all of my premium features. I like the app but I don’t like the pay structure and I don’t like being tricked into paying more when I renew.
Amazing app, only fitness app I actually use. Super Team, super support. 2nd year premium.

I struggle a lot with consistency and an all or nothing attitude. Gentler is very encouraging and is helping to teach me balance with less guilt. For someone with ADHD and body issues this can be really hard but the prompts are kind and don’t cause shame when I haven’t slept well and lack energy

The app is Still having Bugs bugs.
When you start your workout it’s takes 7-8 minutes for the app to start counting your heart bits …. Ordinary

I like the idea of this app, but think it’s a little expensive for what it is, the functionality is quite basic imo, it’s essentially a few clever charts. I also wish there were more widget options (like of the different charts), and a way to start workouts from shortcuts, which I use on my watch with the native Workout app all the time.

title.label: Love the app, please bring back Apple Watch widget

content.label: I love the app, I pay for the yearly membership, but today the small watch face widget for seeing your status and starting a workout disappeared. I can’t add it back 😔
Trust me I tried them all. This one worked for me.

title.label: The iPhone app is nice, but…

content.label: The iPhone app is nice, but I wish there was a watch app for my garmin.
I rated this one star two years ago and I just started using it again. The updates have been amazing and the information it gives you is very helpful. I changed my rating to 5 stars!

Just received my email notification for renewal. Super excited to be renewing this app! Totally worth every penny. 

This app provides balance and lets me know if I’m overdoing it. It’s much kinder than Apple’s rings. I can take a sick day and not feel guilty. ☺️❤️
Maybe I have not gotten used to it enough but I don’t see the real advantage to it.

title.label: No Recommendations for Post menopausal women

content.label: Yes, I am still learning this app (~6 weeks). But I had been a a FitBit user for over 2 years prior. In a comparison, I think Apple’s system is more user friendly, has more options and seamlessly coordinates with my Apple phone and iPad. So far, I am doing well with the daily basics on activity, nutrition and sleep. But the app appears to be missing a larger female group; the post menopausal female users. I’ve been very active throughout my life as a professional dancer, fitness, instructor, post secondary instructor/director for a university dance faculty. And I have pursued outdoor activities over my lifetime, such as downhill skiing hiking, biking, running, and much more. I’ve never had a weight problem of concern; Only a slight menopausal weight gain that has levelled off. Why not include a focus group for post menopausal women, like your focus group for women who have periods? We are overlooked in this area of Apple Watches.

It’s frustrating, as this has been reported in detail months ago and has been ignored. If you record a workout closely after another, it ignores the second workout. This often means that it will only count a 2 minute workout and discard a 45 minute workout, even if they overlap by only 1 second. It’s so illogical for such an otherwise well made app for this to be ignored.

After a hard workout, this app was recommended to me. I’m disabled, so working out is hard for me. I downloaded this app, allowed it to see my most recent workout (it was a dance workout)…and then it said my exertion was “extremely light.” 😑 Instant bad feelings, because it was super hard for me to do and I was panting like crazy. Oh, do you want to change that and tell how you thought it really was? Well, you can do that!…if you pay money. That was the moment I deleted the app. I guilt myself enough. I don’t need a fitness app doing it, too.

title.label: Truly brings value to Apple Health data

content.label: If this app does nothing more it definitely helps humanise Apple Health Data. Making it relatable and actionable. Thank you for creating this app and motivating me to move but also take care. Love Yorhart :)

This is hands down the best workout app I’ve used to date. I’ve been using it for about three months now and have seen a marked improvement in my running speed and endurance. I’ve been running avidly for 15 years and always having to take breaks from injuries. Having insights into how my body is recovering from runs and guidance on how hard to push has seen me make more progress COMFORTABLY than I’ve ever made in the past. Highly recommend!

title.label: Better than the native workout app

content.label: Gentler streak is AMAZING. I can’t say enough about them. I have recommended the app to all my friends and it’s so much better than the rings system Apple has. This app is tailored for YOU and gives super valuable insights into your body and how you are improving your fitness and how different things of your health effect your recovery. I really can’t say enough about this app. The subscription is VERY reasonable for what you get and you also get the option to record many other workouts that the default fitness app doesn’t have. 100/10 would recommend to EVERYONE

I have found this app to be almost entirely unhelpful. It constantly says I am overreaching, because it does not know how to interpret the data it is receiving for example, I have the Peloton app, and if I do gentle stretching, or a yin yoga class, or even meditation in that app, the gentler streak app thinks that I’ve done a hard-core workout and tells me that I’m doing too much. It really is basically useless.
I have a new iWatch, this app has been popping up to try but it will not connect to my iWatch, all other apps do.

title.label: Great app disappointed it’s not compatible with my watch

content.label: I’m really enjoying the app, but I was really excited about having it on my Apple Watch as well. Sadly, it’s not compatible with series 3 Apple Watch. I was quite disappointed by this, not everybody can afford the latest version of the Apple Watch. It would’ve been nice to be included.

I love this app and I love how the people behind it are answering questions.

The graphics are beautiful and using the app is very intuitive.

They deserve their « app of the year » mention.

The annual fee is surprisingly affordable and I really appreciate it.

I highly recommend this app.

This app is simply a delight to use with its beautiful user interface. One of the biggest reasons I love this app is the live heart rate zones. I can see on my phone while working out, which motivates me to push myself further.
Throughout the time using this app, my RHR has gone low and HRV has gone up, which is awesome.

The app is fine except for the fact that ONE workout will trigger at least FOUR push notifications throughout the day. It doesn't matter if you already opened one and checked the workout in the app. No, you will get spammed three more times. Please stop.

Gentler Streak has been a great find for me and my clients. 

I’m living life well now with fibromyalgia and would have really appreciated this app 20 years ago  as I negotiated through life after being athletic before diagnosis. I didn’t/couldn’t move for years. 

Once again I am working on regaining my fitness after a year of concussion recovery. 

I really appreciate everything this app includes. There is a reason it is winning awards. It is so well thought out. Well done.

The wife and I are really enjoying this app we find that we feel better and have more energy fallowing along with our body feedback from the app and you don’t have to kill your self to get there we are both in our 70’s feel 10 years younger! Paul

Gentler Streak is a dream. It helps me focus on improving my overall activity level, without pushing too hard, and without focusing on weight. I was delighted to find that you can’t even add your weight into the app! 

Fitness apps can be ableist and fat phobic, and harmful to your health if you’ve experienced disordered eating. This is the first genuinely safe, positive fitness app I’ve found and it’s helping me actually get moving.

I love the streak view, that helps me see if my activity level is trending up or down over 10 days. It’s perfect for me as a visual learner with ADHD. (I want this for tracking all goals in my life! lol) 

Thank you gentler streak! You’re making the world a better place, please make more apps!

title.label: No trial to get a sense of the app

content.label: While the colors and illustrations are fun to look at, the app is basically pointless unless I pay for it. For me to pay for it, I would like to give it a spin first.

Like the theory behind this but the wrist temp doesn’t seem to work. I wear my Apple Watch all the time yet it doesn’t measure anything. Also how do I keep my longest move streak going if I don’t close my ring? A bit misleading.
Unfortunately very hard to get a sense of the app when 90% of features are behind a pay wall and there’s no free trials available

Seems like it could be OK, but free version doesn’t give you very much and $65/year for a subscription is a lot for a workout app, just to remind you to take it easy once in a while. Maybe there’s some awesomeness I’m not seeing?

title.label: Please provide way to skip the intro

content.label: I don’t keep fitness apps downloaded on my phone to avoid phone addiction. But every time I redownload the app the unskippable intro is too long.

Really liked the idea of the app, however after purchasing the annual subscription whilst on the free trial period - noticed it was continually telling me to rest!
Decided to cancel subscription - but might give another try at later date.

I’m so happy to see Gentler Streak win App of the Year, it’s well deserved. 

Unlike the default Apple Watch ring closing, which encourages you to move or workout even when you’re sick or overtrained, this app gives you recommendations on when to rest while still maintaining your streak. The specific recommended workouts help provide direction for improving fitness at a sustainable pace. 

The annual subscription is very reasonably priced compared to the vast majority of fitness apps that offer you sale prices which are still 2-3x the standard price here. 

My one complaint is that the Watch app’s GPS mapping is absolutely bananas. Not even close. Random straight lines through structures that are often blocks away from my actual route. It’s totally unusable if you want GPS data. (And yet it’s still a 5 star app to me, so imagine how great it would be if it had decent GPS, which the Watch is capable of.)
This is a wonderful tracker for all kinds of activity definitely recommend for people of all abilities Suggestion why is singing not part of physical activity?
